newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds move up, focus on short maturities.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds move up, focus on short maturities.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds moved gently higher in moderately active business on Tuesday with buyers stepping off the sidelines to pick up short maturity paper at the expense of long-dated issues.

"There are a lot of bids in the short end. There is a feeling that short rates went up too far too fast so now people are buying back the paper," one trader said. "It looks like continuing for the coming days."
"In the longer end there is not really selling, but the buying has evaporated. People have stopped the curve flattening trades of recent days," he added.
Traders said there was also some activity in 10-year paper following Monday's auction and with the non-competitive sale later on Tuesday.
However, most players also had one eye on the forthcoming flood of U.S. data, with an array of figures due between Tuesday and the end of the week US-ECI.
Friday's are the most significant, including non-farm payrolls, personal spending, factory orders and the National Association of Purchasing Managers index.
Money market rates, which have been climbing steadily for the past week, paused for a breather on Tuesday.
Traders said the market was still at a loss to explain why the National Bank of Belgium was continuing to drain liquidity.
"If there is a reason, we should know. If there isn't then it should stop," one trader said.
The one-week repo rate was unchanged from late Monday at 4.05/15 percent.
The benchmark 10-year OLO was yielding 5.62 percent at 0910 GMT against 5.65 percent late on Monday. The spread over German Bunds was 10 basis points against nine.
The front month futures contract was 20 basis points higher at 122.00.
